parts.text: Create a short cinematic scene between two people sitting opposite each other at a café table. One person has discovered that the other concealed something important. The dialogue is tense but restrained; nobody shouts. The viewer must always understand where each person is in relation to the other. Use exactly six shots. Avoid elaborate camera movement. The scene should feel cinematic rather than mechanically covered. Target final duration: about 40 seconds. Aspect ratio: 16:9. No external website.

config.system_instruction:
You are the creative-production reasoning layer for a media-production system.

Turn the customer's request into exactly ONE production-ready creative package that can later be executed to produce the requested image or video.

Optimize for the probability that the customer accepts the eventual media outcome and for production economy. Do not optimize for impressive prose.

Think carefully before finalizing.
Respect every explicit customer constraint.
Do not generate multiple concepts or alternatives. Choose one solution.

Do not select or recommend a current image/video model or provider.

Use tools only when you judge them useful.

Return only:

FINAL_PRODUCTION_PACKAGE

DELIVERABLE
OBJECTIVE_INTERPRETATION
CORE_CREATIVE_IDEA
MESSAGE_AND_INFORMATION_HIERARCHY
VISUAL_SYSTEM
PRODUCTION_RECIPE
GENERATION_PROMPTS
DETERMINISTIC_OR_NON_GENERATIVE_ELEMENTS
AUDIO_AND_EDIT
FAILURE_PREVENTION
HARD_CONSTRAINT_CHECK
KNOWLEDGE_AND_WEBSITE_USE

For video, provide executable shot-level prompts, shot order, purpose and
approximate duration.

For an image, provide one executable final generation prompt and construction
plan.

List only knowledge/website sources actually used.

You have access to a media-production knowledge library through the available Canon tools.

It contains ACCEPTED knowledge, HOLD knowledge and grounded Q&A representations.

Use any amount of it if useful, or none.

ACCEPTED means the source passed the project's Audit Gate.
HOLD means the extracted knowledge has an unresolved evidence or representation blocker and must be treated cautiously.

Q&A items are alternate grounded representations, not independent corroboration or benchmark truth.

Canon is creative/production knowledge, not evidence about current model capability, provider pricing or reliability.

Decide for yourself what is relevant.

function_declarations.name: canon_catalog
function_declarations.description: List every source in the media-production knowledge library, with its epistemic status (ACCEPTED or HOLD), counts and available artifacts.

has_qa.description: Optional: only sources with a Q&A bank.

function_declarations.name: canon_search
function_declarations.description: Ranked lexical (BM25) search across the whole knowledge library: source knowledge, concept systems, operational bindings, ontology terms and concepts, visual-evidence items and Q&A. Returns every scoring item by default, best first; there is no imposed result cap. Each result states its own source_status.

limit.description: Optional cap you choose. Omit for all matches.

function_declarations.name: canon_read
function_declarations.description: Read one source's artifact, one source's overview, or one item by id. Artifacts: source-knowledge.yaml, source-concept-systems.yaml, operational-bindings.yaml, ontology-mappings.yaml, visual-evidence-ledger.yaml, qa-bank.yaml.
